_comment: R-124 PURGE principal: delete an EXACT version, and only after Object Lock
has expired. COMPLIANCE mode is what actually enforces the timing — no
principal, including the account root, can delete a locked version — so
this policy grants the verb and the lock supplies the clock.
s3:BypassGovernanceRetention is deliberately absent and is denied again by
the bucket policy. Mirrored by `JournalPurgeTransport`, whose only method
is deleteObjectVersion and which refuses an empty version id (a delete
without one writes a delete marker instead of removing anything).

The purge job READS before it deletes: journal-purge.ts verifies each chain and refuses to purge one that does not verify, because a damaged chain is evidence and evidence is not garbage-collected. That requires s3:GetObjectVersion. Granting it here keeps the verb split that matters -- this principal still cannot CREATE, and the writer still cannot DELETE (round-1 security M2 / tenancy C3).
